subject.title: [Bug]: project-local .env is ignored in 2026.3.28, OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH falls back to ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json

question: Should untrusted workspace `.env` files be allowed to set `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, or should the current fail-closed `OPENCLAW_*` workspace boundary remain the product policy?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally block the whole `OPENCLAW_*` namespace from workspace `.env`, while this issue reports a real regression from the earlier raw dotenv behavior; automation cannot choose that security tradeoff safely.

options.title: Keep the fail-closed boundary
options.body: Keep blocking `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` in workspace `.env`, point users to process/global trusted env, and close or retitle this issue as an intentional security tradeoff.

options.title: Allow a narrow config-path exception
options.body: Permit only `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` from workspace `.env`, keep `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` blocked, and update tests and docs to name the accepted trust model.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Add a visible operator-controlled opt-in for workspace config-path selection instead of enabling it by default.

recommendation.title: Keep the fail-closed boundary
recommendation.body: Keep blocking `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` in workspace `.env`, point users to process/global trusted env, and close or retitle this issue as an intentional security tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the filtered workspace dotenv boundary that caused the reported regression, so they are the best history-backed routing candidate for the security tradeoff.
